content: Silver sulfadiazine is a sulfa-based medication that is specifically used to prevent and treat infections in secondand third-degree burns. It works by eliminating a broad spectrum of bacteria. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. This medication is available in the form of a cream. It is typically applied once or twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and if you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use silver sulfadiazine exactly as prescribed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than directed by your doctor. It should not be used on infants under 2 months of age. Continue using the medication until your doctor advises you to stop, as the burn must heal completely to prevent infection. Clean the burned area gently every day to remove dead skin. If the burn becomes infected or the infection worsens, contact your doctor immediately. Before applying the cream, clean the affected area thoroughly and remove any dead or burned tissue. Always wear a sterile, disposable glove when applying the cream. Cover the cleaned burn with a layer of cream approximately 1/16-inch thick. Before using silver sulfadiazine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to silver sulfadiazine, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Silver sulfadiazine may cause mild side effects, such as pain, burning, or itching. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects may include unusual bleeding or bruising, fever, sore throat, yellowing of the skin or eyes, blood in the urine, joint pain, extreme fatigue or weakness, or a skin rash. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Silver sulfadiazine is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply any dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless instructed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If your skin condition worsens or does not improve, inform your doctor. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Silver sulfadiazine is available under the brand names Silvadene®, SSD Cream®, and Thermazene®.
